ch11_lab_git.title: Quick Check: Git, GitHub & the Command Line

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between Git and GitHub?
options: They are the exact same tool with two names
Git is the local Version Control System software installed on your laptop; GitHub is the online cloud hub where you store and share that history with a team
GitHub is installed locally; Git is the cloud website
Git only works for JavaScript, GitHub works for all languages

questions.q: Which Git command downloads a full copy of a remote repository (files + complete history) when you're joining a project for the first time?
options: git pull
git clone
git push
git init

questions.q: What causes a Merge Conflict in Git?
options: Two developers used different variable names
Two branches changed the exact same line of the same file, so Git can't automatically decide which version to keep
A developer forgot to run git init
The internet connection dropped during a push

ch11_lab_cloud.title: Quick Check: Cloud Computing & Data Centers

questions.q: "The Cloud" is often called a nickname because it actually refers to what?
options: A weather pattern that affects internet speed
Physical computers (servers) inside secured Data Center buildings, rented over the internet
A single supercomputer owned by one company
Software that has no physical hardware at all

questions.q: Why does Linux dominate web server hosting compared to Windows Server?
options: Windows Server can't connect to the internet
Linux is free/open-source with no per-server license fee, is extremely stable under heavy traffic, and has a massive community patching security holes
Linux only works on Apple computers
Windows Server is actually more popular for hosting

questions.q: Which of the 'Big Three' cloud providers is described as 'the Original & the Biggest,' hosting Netflix and Twitch?
options: Azure (Microsoft)
AWS (Amazon Web Services)
GCP (Google Cloud Platform)
None of the Big Three host video streaming

questions.q: In the 'Pizza as a Service' analogy, which cloud service model gives you a fully stocked kitchen where you just bring your code and 'cook' (deploy), without managing hardware or the OS?
options: IaaS (you rent the raw dough/hardware)
PaaS (the kitchen is stocked, you just cook)
SaaS (you just eat at a restaurant)
On-Premises (you own the whole restaurant)

questions.q: A bank keeps sensitive customer data in a locked private server but runs its public blog on cheap shared hosting. What deployment model is this?
options: Public Cloud
Private Cloud
Hybrid Cloud
IaaS

questions.q: What is the key difference between Scalability and Elasticity?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Scalability is the ability to add power as demand grows; Elasticity also includes automatically scaling BACK DOWN when demand drops, to save money
Scalability only applies to storage; Elasticity only applies to CPU
Elasticity means the site never needs more servers
